content.summary_of_the_paper:
In  this manuscript, authors propose a transformer-based method for burst image processing, which incorporates multi-level local-global burst feature alignment and adaptive burst feature aggregation. The contributions of this manuscript mainly consist of the following two points:
1, The model of the proposed method is efficient and lightweight compared with existing SOTA methods.
2, Both the quantitative and qualitative results on super-resolution and low-light enhancement are competitive.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1,  The model of the proposed method is efficient and lightweight compared with existing SOTA methods.
2, Both the quantitative and qualitative results on super-resolution and low-light enhancement are competitive. 

Weakness:
1, The novelty of this manuscript is limited and unconvincing to be accepted. Specifically, the rationality and efficiency of some proposed modules have not be demonstrated clearly. For example, in the BFF module of Fig. 2, the rationality of the subtraction is contradictory with the claim in section 3.1.2. Besides, in the ablation study of Table 2,  the effectiveness of the CBS mechanism is unconvincing enough, because there is just 0.12dB performance decrease when disable the mechanism.
2, In the experiment part, authors adopted the reported results of their compared methods in the super-resolution and low-light image enhancement scenarios. However, when comparing the performance of denoising, the performance of the compared methods has a decrease compared with their reported performance on the same dataset. For example, the performance of the BIPNet (Dudhane et al. CVPR 2022) on the grayscale burst denosing is 41.26dB, which is better than this proposed method, however, in Table 5, the performance of BIPNet is changed into 39.28dB, which is worse than the proposed method.
3, The network structure of the proposed method looks very messy and complicated, which makes it seem less elegant. Meanwhile, the writing style, experiment design, and even the tables and graphs in the experiment part is very similar to the BIPNet (Dudhane et al. CVPR 2022), which also makes the novelty of this manuscript limited.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The framework of this manuscript is effective and efficient for the Burst image restoration, and many design details are given to support the reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the experimental results are attractive, the novelty of the proposed is limited and unconvincing to be accepted. Many proposed modules are thin in rationality. And experiment on denoising is unconvincing.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes a transformer-based framework for burst image processing, namely Burstormer. To  recover a high-quality image from the given burst of noisy shots having pixel misalignments, the author critically presents to enable inter-frame communication in the burst neighborhoods for information aggregation and progressive fusion. Specifically, Burstormer employs a multi-scale hierarchical enhanced deformable alignment module (EDA) for aligning burst features to the reference frame and applies the no-reference feature enrichment NRFE and upsampling modules for image reconstruction. Finally, the proposed Burstormer outperforms the existing SOTA approaches on three popular tasks burst super-resolution, burst denoising, and burst low-light enhancement. 

The contribution can be summarized as:
1. Burstormer, a Transformer based framework for burst-image restoration and enhancement that leverages multi-scale local and non-local features for improved alignment and feature fusion.
2. A enhanced deformable alignment module based on the multi-scale hierarchical design that effectively denoises and aligns burst features and also refines features with a reference-based feature enrichment module. 
3. A no-reference feature enrichment module to aggregate and upsample the burst features with less computational overhead. To enable inter-frame interactions, it generates burst neighborhoods through the proposed cyclic burst sampling mechanism.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
+ Strengths 
Reasonable method design and clear writing. The paper contributes a transformer-based scheme Burstormer for burst image processing, which enables inter-frame communication and generate a single high-quality image from a given burst of noisy images with pixel misalignments. Burstormer leverages multi-scale local and non-local features for improved alignment and feature fusion. And the proposed method outperforms the state of the arts approaches BIPNet and EBFA , also showing a high generalizability.

- Weaknesses
There are some problems in experimental design and writing, which must be solved before it is considered for publication. If the following problems are well-addressed, this reviewer believes that the essential contribution of this paper are important for burst image processing. 
● LPIPS in Burst Super-resolution
Prior works [Deep Burst Super-Resolution, Burst Image Restoration and Enhancement] used the LPIPS metric which has been shown to match human perseption well, in addition to PSNR and SSIM to assess the accuracy of superscore results. The problem in this section is lack of sufficient explanation of the  experiment results to prove the proposed method is the best in Burst  SR. 
●  Need more discussion on the limitations of the proposed method.
●  Need more discussion on the Application on edge devices, such as cell phones and pad.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Building on existing approaches, the framework proposed in this paper addresses a research question with a novel approach. Although ideas such as multi-scale local and non-local features have been applied in many articles, this paper is innovative in transferring them to the  burst image processing domain.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I vote for accepting. Compared to existing approaches, Burstormer is more accurate, light-weight and faster. The paper is well written. The idea of  inter-frame communication is interesting and useful. Hopefully the authors can address my concern in the rebuttal period.

content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. This paper is well written and easy to understand. 
2. This paper achieved SOTA performance on various tasks.

Weakness:
1. The major considersion is that the contribution is limited.
(1) For the first contribution: "Transformer based design for burst-image restoration". The transformer structure has been wildly use in image restoration, e.g., SwinIR[1], Restormer[2] ..... Directly utilizing transformer structure in an other task is not a nice contribution. Also, the network structure of transformer is not well discribed in the network section (Figure 2). 
(2) For the second contribution, the enhanced deformable alignment seems represent that the alignment module utilize multi-scale structure. However, it is also well discussed in other paper, i.e., EDVR [3] (video SR), GCP-Net [4] (burst restoration). Thus this is also not a contribution.
(3) The third contribution (enrichment module) is new but is not a novelty enough.

2. In table 2, This paper should also compare with the PCD align module in [3] and [4] to show the efficient of the proposed enhanced alighment module.

3. Some experiment seems strange. In figure 3 (b), we can see the input base frame is overexposure in the select box position. However, the ground-truth and the result of this paper is well  exposured. Why the netowrk can adjust the exposure statement? Why other methods can not adjust the input exposure? I think it exist some unfair comparision.

[1] Liang, Jingyun, et al. "Swinir: Image restoration using swin transformer." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision. 2021.
[2] Zamir, Syed Waqas, et al. "Restormer: Efficient transformer for high-resolution image restoration." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2022.
[3] Wang, Xintao, et al. "Edvr: Video restoration with enhanced deformable convolutional networks." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops. 2019.
[4] Guo, Shi, Zhetong Liang, and Lei Zhang. "Joint denoising and demosaicking with green channel prior for real-world burst images." IEEE Transactions on Image Processing 30 (2021): 6930-6942.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a transformer-based architecture for burst image restoration and enhancement. It consists of two main steps: alignment and reconstruction. The alignment is carried out  on different image scales, where in each scale the alignment is based on deformable convolutions and "feature enrichment" for refinement. Once aligned, the image reconstruction is done by sampling the pixels from different frames.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
* Strengths:
1. The problem of alignment in burst images is still an open problem, particularly when the camera motion is large or when objects in the scene move faster than the camera's shutter speed.

* Weaknesses:
1. The paper is difficult to read. Many sentences use self-invented jargon that the meaning is unclear.  For example: "incorporates multi-level local-global burst feature alignment and adaptive burst feature aggregation". There is no discussion on what it means by local-global or by adaptive feature aggregation. Another example: "allow a one go interaction with the reference frame during the alignment process, we add a new reference-based feature enrichment (RBFE) mechanism in EDA to allow a more extensive interaction with the reference frame." What it means by "one go interaction" or "extensive interaction" is not explained. Many sentences are like these examples, which make the paper significantly difficult to understand.

2. The pipeline in Fig.(2) looks considerably complex. It is not immediately clear where the novelties are. The multiscale operation is commonly used. Deformable convolutions have been used in image alignment. RBFE and BFF might be new, but it is unclear what they are theoretically contributing and why they work better than simple CNNs. The same applies to the reconstruction part. Basically, it is unclear why the proposed module for reconstruction needs to be constructed in that way. There are no proper theoretical justifications in the paper.

3. While the ablation studies show the effectiveness of RBFE, it is unclear theoretically why it works. What does enrichment here mean? 

4. The enhanced deformable alignment module is very similar to EBFA from BIPNet and FEPCD from this paper below. FEPCD also utilises the multi-level hierarchical architecture and deformable convolutions for burst alignment.
Luo Z, Yu L, Mo X, et al. EBSR: Feature enhanced burst super-resolution with deformable alignment, CVPR 2021

5. In the reconstruction part, the proposed NRFE is claimed to be novel. However, it is similar to a pseudo-burst feature fusion (PBFF) from BIPNet. In theory, if we replace NRFE with PBFF, is there any significant degradation in terms of the performance?

6. The performance improvements in Tables 1, 3, 4, and particularly 5, 6 are marginal.

7. Some results in Table 6 are wrong. The average PSNR of MFIR on the colour denoising dataset is 37.40 (not 37.13 as the paper claims). That of BIPNet is 38.74 (not 37.20 as the paper claims). Comparing these correct numbers with the proposed method's result, which is 37.59, as mentioned, the improvement is marginal and even lower than BIPNet.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is lack of novelty. The paper is difficult to understand. The improvement is marginal.

content.title: Burstormer: Burst Image Restoration and Enhancement Transformer
content.abstract:
On a shutter press, modern handheld cameras capture multiple images in rapid succession and merge them to generate a single image. However, individual frames in a burst are misaligned due to inevitable motions and contain multiple degradations. The challenge is to properly align the successive image shots and merge their complimentary information to achieve high-quality outputs. Towards this direction, we propose Burstormer: a novel transformer-based architecture for burst image restoration and enhancement. In comparison to existing works, our approach exploits multi-scale local and non-local features to achieve improved alignment and feature fusion. Our key idea is to enable inter-frame communication in the burst neighborhoods for information aggregation and progressive fusion while modeling the burst-wide context. However, the input burst frames need to be properly aligned before fusing their information. Therefore, we propose an enhanced deformable alignment module for aligning burst features with regards to the reference frame. Unlike existing techniques, the proposed alignment module not only aligns burst features but also exchanges feature information and maintains focused communication with the reference frame through the proposed reference-based feature enrichment mechanism. This additional exchange of information helps in aligning multi-frame features under complex motions. After multi-level alignment and enrichment, we re-emphasize on inter-frame communication within burst frames using a new cyclic burst sampling technique. Finally, the inter-frame information is aggregated using our proposed burst feature fusion module followed by progressive increase in the spatial resolution by shuffling the feature information available in burst frames. The proposed Burstormer outperforms the existing state-of-the-art approaches on three popular tasks of burst super-resolution, burst denoising and burst low-light enhancement. Our codes will
be made public.
